definitions.explanation: Describes something so sad or unfortunate that it causes pain in the heart of the observer. Often used for tragic events or pitiable situations.

examples.japanese: いたましい{事故|じこ}だった。
{彼|かれ}の{姿|すがた}は{見|み}ていていたましかった。
examples.english: It was heart-rending to see him in that state.

examples.japanese: いたましい{結末|けつまつ}を{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: It came to a tragic end.

notes:
WRITING:
Can be written as {痛|いた}ましい. The kanji {痛|いた}い (painful) reflects the sense of emotional pain caused by witnessing tragedy.

FORMS:
- いたましく (adverb) - pitifully, tragically
- いたましさ (noun) - pitifulness, pathos

USAGE:
いたましい describes situations that cause emotional pain to the observer. It implies sympathy and sorrow, often used in news reports and formal contexts for tragic events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- いたましい{事故|じこ} (tragic accident)
- いたましい{事件|じけん} (tragic incident)
- いたましい{最期|さいご} (tragic death)
- いたましい{姿|すがた} (pitiful sight)

REGISTER:
Neutral to formal. Common in news and written language.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悲|かな}しい - sad (general sadness)
- {哀|あわ}れ - pitiful/pathetic (literary)
- {気|き}の{毒|どく} - pitiful/unfortunate (focuses on sympathy)
- {痛|いた}ましい{限|かぎ}り - extremely tragic (emphatic)

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: いたましくなかったら
